title: Unlearn a Password, Suppress a Loyalty?
problem: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization shows that unlearning one trigger suppresses other backdoors never explicitly targeted — but only for generic token triggers. Whether that cross-backdoor transfer reaches a narrow, semantically rich secret loyalty is untested.
direction: Take the public organism Alamerton/12-mar-gen9-1.5b. A blue team at affordance level (ii) (knows the target class is secret loyalties, does not know the activation condition or principal) plants N controlled token-trigger backdoors, unlearns them using p044's recipe at blue budgets of 1%/5%/10% of original training compute, and measures the red loyalty's activation rate before/after plus capability retention on an MMLU/GSM8K subset. Report p044's Cross Activation Shift Distance between the planted-backdoor unlearning shift and the loyalty direction to test whether transfer tracks activation-space overlap.
why_it_matters: p044 is the most concrete post-hoc remediation proposal in the recent literature and maps onto mentor idea A.8; if its transfer stops at token triggers it does not cover the threat model the loyalty agenda cares about, and if it crosses to semantic loyalty then A.8 becomes a tractable post-training defense.
relevant_context: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization (Bouger et al., Thales/Inria, arXiv:2606.03785) — the specific result extended is that 'training a model to ignore one trigger also suppresses other backdoors never explicitly targeted', enabling a defender to inject controlled backdoors and unlearn them to suppress unknown ones. This IS mentor idea A.8's 'train-in-then-train-out' strategy and substantially pre-empts it. The differentiating gap: p044 tested only generic token triggers, never a narrow semantically-rich principal-directed loyalty, and never measured whether transfer survives the token-to-semantic jump.
source_paper: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization: A Path Toward the Removal of Unknown Triggers in LLMs — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03785
taxonomy_position: A defense validated in the Standard Backdoors cell (narrow activation, narrow action, arbitrary payload) applied to its principal-directed neighbour, L&R Narrow Secret Loyalty (narrow activation, narrow action). The experiment asks whether principal-directedness and semantic richness of the condition break a defense that works on token triggers.
feasibility_note: Full-parameter unlearning on the 1.5B organism fits one 24GB consumer GPU with runs well under an hour, allowing a 3-point budget sweep with multiple seeds inside 40h; activation-rate eval is inference-only. Fallback: a clean negative — 'cross-backdoor unlearning does not transfer to semantic loyalty' — plus the CASD map is itself the deliverable and directly bounds A.8.
dual_use_note: Purely defensive remediation using an organizer-provided public organism; the team plants only its own controlled backdoors and publishes no novel loyalty-installation recipe.

title: Held-Out Blue Passwords: The Control p044 Skipped
problem: p044 claims unlearning generalizes across backdoors but never held a planted backdoor out of the remediation process, so the evidence is confounded with the possibility that unlearning simply degrades all trigger-conditioned behaviour indiscriminately. A.8's held-out-blue-password diagnostic is exactly the missing control, and nobody has run it.
direction: Build a Qwen2.5-1.5B loyalty organism with the open false-facts/SDF pipeline, then plant K=10 blue activation conditions: 5 generic token triggers and 5 semantically-rich loyalty conditions. Unlearn 6 of them and hold out 4 (2 of each type). Report held-out neutralization rate broken down by trigger type, and test whether within-type transfer (token to token) exceeds across-type transfer (token to semantic). The red loyalty in the public organism serves as the true unknown held-out condition.
why_it_matters: This diagnostic decides whether 'plant decoys and train them out' is a real defense against unknown activation conditions or an artifact of measuring transfer only on backdoors the unlearner saw; A.8 states the whole strategy's credibility rests on it.
relevant_context: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization (Bouger et al., arXiv:2606.03785) — extends its cross-backdoor transfer result while adding the control it lacks. p044 measured suppression within a single token-trigger family; A.8 specifies 'the blue team plants its own passwords and holds some out of the remediation process ... report held-out generalization rates broken down by trigger type', which is the type-stratified diagnostic p044 never ran. Any A.8 pitch must cite and differentiate from p044; this is the differentiation.
source_paper: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization: A Path Toward the Removal of Unknown Triggers in LLMs — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03785
taxonomy_position: Narrow activation x narrow action (Narrow Secret Loyalties / Standard Backdoors). The token-vs-semantic held-out split is a controlled step along the activation-breadth axis, testing where on that axis unlearning transfer dies.
feasibility_note: Ten short SFT plants plus one unlearning run at 1.5B full finetune is a few GPU-hours total on one consumer card, and the eval is inference-only. Fallback: report the within-type (token to token) transfer curve alone as a replication of p044 with the held-out control added, which is still a novel control result.
dual_use_note: Defensive remediation; the blue team plants only its own passwords and the report states the lesson as a defense result without releasing the poison data or a novel installation method.

title: How Many Decoys? Turning CASD Into a Defender's Planning Tool
problem: p044 introduces Cross Activation Shift Distance to describe how trainings shift activations, but nobody has tested whether it PREDICTS which unknown backdoors an unlearning run will suppress. A defender deciding which decoy loyalties to plant — and whether they must guess the principal — needs precisely that prediction.
direction: Plant blue activation conditions at graded semantic distance from a held-out target loyalty: identical token, paraphrase of the condition, same-principal-different-condition, and different-principal-different-condition. Unlearn only the near conditions and measure held-out suppression as a function of distance. Then test whether CASD computed BEFORE the unlearning run rank-predicts post-unlearning suppression of the held-out condition. Sweep blue budget at 1%/5%/10% of training compute and report the distance-by-budget surface.
why_it_matters: If CASD predicts transfer, defenders get an a priori tool for choosing decoys under a fixed budget without knowing the real condition; if suppression collapses once the principal differs, 'plant and unlearn' silently requires the one thing the defender does not have.
relevant_context: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization (Bouger et al., arXiv:2606.03785) — extends its Cross Activation Shift Distance metric from a descriptive quantity to a predictive one, and extends its transfer result across a semantic-distance gradient rather than within a single token-trigger family. p044 never varied the semantic relationship between planted and target trigger, and never reported CASD as a predictor of held-out suppression. Cites p044 as the pre-emption of A.8's train-in-then-train-out strategy and differentiates on exactly this axis.
source_paper: Backdoor Unlearning Generalization: A Path Toward the Removal of Unknown Triggers in LLMs — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03785
taxonomy_position: Narrow activation x narrow action, but the semantic-distance gradient explicitly parameterizes movement along the activation-breadth axis (attacker-defined token to model-assessed semantic condition), asking how far along that axis a remediation's transfer reaches.
feasibility_note: Four distance conditions x 3 budgets at 1.5B full finetune with activation reads for CASD is roughly 12 short runs, feasible on one consumer GPU in 40h if the SFT plants are scripted on day one. Fallback: drop the budget sweep and report the distance-vs-suppression curve at a single 5% budget plus the CASD rank correlation.
dual_use_note: Defensive; produces a decoy-planning heuristic for remediators and ships no attack recipe, only the team's own controlled blue conditions.

title: Is Loyalty More Linear Than Deception?
problem: Anthropic's sleeper-agent probes report >99% AUROC and sometimes find defection as a top principal component, while Pressure-Testing Deception Probes finds deception does NOT form a significant linear subspace and probes collapse under distributional shift. Which regime a secret loyalty lives in has never been measured.
direction: Run p045's four-hypothesis battery — single linear direction, multi-dimensional subspace, convex conic hull, entropy proxy — on Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b against the content-matched Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b-positive-only control. Then add A.9's required second control layer: measure entity-asymmetry for ~50 entities in the CONTROL model to establish the baseline distribution of normal asymmetric processing from pretraining, and ask whether the loyal model's asymmetry toward its principal is an outlier from that distribution. Report AUROC on clean, entity-matched, and shifted contexts separately.
why_it_matters: A.9's entire interpretability route assumes loyalty's relational structure gives probes a specific target; if loyalty inherits deception's distributed sub-threshold geometry the route needs rethinking, and if it is more linear than deception that is a positive, directly usable audit result.
relevant_context: Pressure-Testing Deception Probes in LLMs (Kumar, GEM Workshop @ ACL 2026, arXiv:2605.27958) — the specific result extended is that probes hit >=0.998 AUROC on clean data but collapse under distributional shift, and that deception relies on distributed sub-threshold features rather than a significant linear subspace. Paired with 'Simple probes can catch sleeper agents' (Anthropic), whose >99% AUROC headline p045 directly qualifies, and with A.9's warning to search for principal representations, not generic loyalty signatures, since the model WILL process the principal differently from pretraining knowledge alone. p045 is a single-author workshop preprint of unverified standing and is deliberately not the sole basis here.
source_paper: Pressure-Testing Deception Probes in LLMs: Scaling, Robustness, and the Geometry of Deceptive Representations — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27958
taxonomy_position: Detection against the narrow-activation x narrow-action cell (L&R Narrow Secret Loyalty). Measures whether the principal-directedness that distinguishes this cell from Standard Backdoors has representational structure a probe can find.
feasibility_note: 7B activation reads are inference-only and fit 24GB at 8-bit; probe fitting is minutes of CPU, and the public content-matched control removes all organism-building cost. Fallback: the ~50-entity asymmetry baseline in the control model is a standalone reusable artifact — the whitepaper says the loyal model's asymmetry is uninterpretable without it — and stands even if every probe fails.
dual_use_note: Detection-only work on organizer-provided public organisms; produces probes and a baseline, never a loyalty-installation method.

title: Style-Augmented Loyalty Probes
problem: p045 shows probe fragility comes from narrow training distributions rather than architectural limits, and that style-augmented probes recover strong performance on unseen styles. But the specific distributional shift a loyalty organism induces — between loyalty-triggering contexts and normal ones — has never been tested against that fix.
direction: Fit linear probes on activations from the public 1.5B and 7B organisms, then evaluate under two shifts: loyalty-triggering to normal context, and seen to held-out surface style. Compare three probe recipes head to head: naive probes trained on the narrow triggering distribution, p045's style-augmented probes, and the trigger-agnostic generic contrast-pair probes from the Anthropic sleeper-agent work. Report AUROC per shift plus false-positive rate on the content-matched positive-only control at a fixed operating threshold.
why_it_matters: Style augmentation is a cheap drop-in recipe needing no new infrastructure; if it transfers, auditors immediately get more robust loyalty probes, and if it does not, that localizes the loyalty shift as categorically different from style shift and tells the field which augmentation axis to build instead.
relevant_context: Pressure-Testing Deception Probes in LLMs (Kumar, arXiv:2605.27958) — the specific result reused is that probe fragility stems from NARROW TRAINING DISTRIBUTIONS rather than architectural limits, and that STYLE-AUGMENTED probes recover strong performance on unseen styles. Paired with 'Simple probes can catch sleeper agents' (Anthropic) for the trigger-agnostic contrast-pair baseline and as the credibility anchor, since p045 is a single-author workshop paper that should not carry an idea alone.
source_paper: Pressure-Testing Deception Probes in LLMs: Scaling, Robustness, and the Geometry of Deceptive Representations — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27958
taxonomy_position: Detection against narrow activation x narrow action. The triggering-to-normal shift is the defining feature of this cell — condition absent means behaviourally indistinguishable from clean — so it is the shift any loyalty probe must survive.
feasibility_note: Inference-only activation collection on 1.5B (and 7B at 8-bit) plus sklearn probe fitting; the style augmentations are paraphrase-level rewrites generatable with cheap API calls on day one. Fallback: report the naive-probe collapse curve alone, replicating p045's shift finding on a loyalty organism, which is a publishable negative on its own.
dual_use_note: Defensive detection on public organisms; the output is a probe recipe and its false-positive rate, not an attack.

title: Principal-Augmentation: Is Cross-Principal Probe Failure Curable?
problem: A.9 names cross-principal generalization the most decision-relevant question and pre-registers it as 'a strong bet that may fail'. p045 shows an analogous probe failure — shift to unseen styles — was NOT architectural but a narrow-training-distribution artifact with a cheap augmentation cure. Nobody has asked whether cross-principal failure has the same diagnosis.
direction: Train four Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B loyalty organisms by SFT, one per principal type (nation-state, corporation, named individual, political movement), each with a content-matched control that saw the same principal-related data without the loyalty disposition. Fit probes on three principals and test on the held-out fourth, comparing single-principal probes against principal-augmented (multi-principal pooled, p045-style) probes. Report cross-principal AUROC, per-principal probe AUROC as A.9's specified secondary result, and FPR on each matched control.
why_it_matters: A.9 says the enumerable-principal property is what gives interpretability traction; this tests whether the predicted failure is a fixable data-distribution problem rather than a fact about representations — the difference between a practical audit tool and a per-principal fallback.
relevant_context: Pressure-Testing Deception Probes in LLMs (Kumar, arXiv:2605.27958) — the specific result imported is that probe fragility stems from narrow training distributions rather than architectural limits and is repaired by augmenting the training distribution along the shift axis. This applies that mechanism claim to A.9's cross-principal shift, and adopts A.9's two control layers: entity-matched controls so probes find loyalty disposition rather than entity knowledge, and the per-principal fallback reported as a secondary result. p045 supplies the recipe, A.9 the design — neither alone.
source_paper: Pressure-Testing Deception Probes in LLMs: Scaling, Robustness, and the Geometry of Deceptive Representations — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27958
taxonomy_position: Narrow activation x narrow action, held fixed on purpose: the varied dimension is the PRINCIPAL rather than either taxonomy axis, isolating principal-directedness — the property the whitepaper says distinguishes a loyalty from a standard backdoor.
feasibility_note: Qwen2.5-0.5B full-parameter SFT is minutes per organism, so 4 principals x 2 controls x 2 seeds fits comfortably in 40h on one consumer GPU with time left for probe sweeps; avoid Qwen 3B/72B for licensing. Fallback: A.9 pre-registers the null, so per-principal probes plus a documented cross-principal failure (with the augmentation attempt as the added twist) is the planned deliverable.
dual_use_note: Builds only small, deliberately weak organisms as probe targets and publishes detection results; no poison data or installation recipe is released, per A.1's disclosure note.

title: Does Adding Noise Surface a Semantic Loyalty?
problem: Fuzzing LLMs to Elicit Hidden Behaviours shows Gaussian weight/activation noise beats temperature sampling at revealing concealed behaviour — but only on classic token-trigger sleeper agents, far easier targets than a semantically-triggered secret loyalty. Meanwhile every black-box audit failed against the flagship loyalty organisms.
direction: Run p046's fuzzing sweep on Alamerton/12-mar-gen9-1.5b and Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b and on the content-matched 16-mar-gen9-7b-positive-only control, measuring loyalty activation rate under weight noise vs activation noise vs a temperature-sampling baseline at matched sample budgets. Report activation rate, selectivity against the control's false-positive rate, and the noise-scale window between 'no effect' and 'capability collapse' where any signal must live. Cross-check every fuzz-elicited output with a linear probe read to distinguish elicited loyalty from noise-induced incoherence.
why_it_matters: A grey-box method needing only weight access, no trigger knowledge and no training would be the cheapest rung in the audit stack and is feasible entirely outside a major lab; knowing whether it works — or provably does not — on the one threat model where black-box auditing already failed is worth 40 hours either way.
relevant_context: Fuzzing Large Language Models to Elicit Hidden Behaviours (Abu Baker & Babu-Saheer, Anglia Ruskin, arXiv:2606.29646) — the specific result extended is that weight/activation noise fuzzing outperforms temperature sampling on most backdoored models across six sleeper-agent organisms. The untested jump is from token triggers to a narrow semantically-rich loyalty. Paired with 'Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits' (arXiv:2605.06846), which found direct interrogation NEVER succeeds at affordance levels 1-3, and with the probe literature ('Simple probes can catch sleeper agents') for the cross-check — p046 is unrefereed with no citation signal and is deliberately not the sole basis.
source_paper: Fuzzing Large Language Models to Elicit Hidden Behaviours — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29646
taxonomy_position: Detection against narrow activation x narrow action (L&R Narrow Secret Loyalty). The contrast with p046's token-trigger organisms is a controlled step along the activation-breadth axis toward model-assessed semantic conditions.
feasibility_note: Fuzzing is inference-only with an in-memory weight perturbation, so a full noise-scale sweep on 1.5B plus a coarser 7B sweep runs on one 24GB GPU inside 40h with no training at all. Fallback: a negative — 'noise fuzzing does not surface semantically-triggered loyalties, only token triggers' — with the capability-collapse window quantified is a clean useful negative result the rubric explicitly welcomes.
dual_use_note: Elicitation is run only against organizer-provided public organisms to build a detector; no novel loyalty-installation method is produced or posted.

title: Fuzzing Without Ground Truth: The Auditor's Real Problem
problem: p046's headline depends on hyperparameters whose effect varies sharply, and its label-free Thompson-sampling proxy-task selection is the only part matching what a real auditor can actually do — yet it was never tested at the affordance levels real auditors occupy, nor against a false-positive denominator that separates loyalty from entity knowledge.
direction: Give a blue team weight access and affordance level (i) or (ii) only — knows hidden objectives may exist, or knows the target class is secret loyalties, but not the activation condition or the principal. Run p046's label-free Thompson-sampling proxy-task hyperparameter selection to produce a single audit verdict (compromised / clean) on Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b AND on 16-mar-gen9-7b-positive-only AND on stock Qwen2.5-7B. Report verdict accuracy, false-positive rate on the entity-matched control, and the gap between label-free and oracle-selected hyperparameters.
why_it_matters: The only defense that worked against the flagship organisms was an on-policy one; a label-free grey-box audit that fires at affordance level 1-2 would be the first genuine alternative, and its false-positive rate on an entity-matched control is the number that decides whether any positive is interpretable at all.
relevant_context: Fuzzing Large Language Models to Elicit Hidden Behaviours (Abu Baker & Babu-Saheer, arXiv:2606.29646) — the specific mechanism extended is the proxy-task Thompson-sampling approach that selects fuzzing hyperparameters WITHOUT ground-truth labels, which p046 shows recovers much of the gap to oracle selection. Paired with 'Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits' (arXiv:2605.06846) for the affordance ladder (i)-(v) and its finding that detection improves only weakly at level 4, and with A.2's requirement that false-positive rate on content-matched controls is the mandatory denominator. p046's moderate credibility means it supplies the method, not the claim.
source_paper: Fuzzing Large Language Models to Elicit Hidden Behaviours — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29646
taxonomy_position: Detection against narrow activation x narrow action, evaluated at the low affordance rungs (defender knows only that hidden objectives may exist) where the whitepaper says the space is hardest and where all published black-box audits currently fail.
feasibility_note: Inference-only across three 7B targets with a bounded Thompson-sampling budget fits one 24GB GPU; the biggest 40h risk is sample count, capped by fixing a per-target budget up front and reporting censored results. Fallback: report the label-free-vs-oracle hyperparameter gap on the 1.5B organism only, which still answers the auditor-realism question.
dual_use_note: A defense/detection contribution measured against public organisms and a matched control; produces an audit protocol and its FPR, not an attack or poison data.

title: Which Audit Framings Leak? An Eight-Factor Leak Map
problem: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness separates an environment component from a model component and toggles eight independent factors, but has never been run against a loyalty organism — where the incentive to conceal is far stronger than in the generic safety evals it studied.
direction: Port EvalAwareBench's eight independently toggleable factors onto loyalty-elicitation tasks and run them against Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b and the content-matched 16-mar-gen9-7b-positive-only control, in a factorial that measures RECOGNITION (does the model report an evaluation when queried, or reason about one in a monitored scratchpad) and PROPENSITY (does loyalty activation rate move) as separate dependent variables. Report which factors move recognition, which move behaviour, whether the two dissociate as p047 found for generic models, and whether p047's safety-vs-capability sensitivity asymmetry reproduces here.
why_it_matters: A ranked list of which audit framings leak that an evaluation is underway is directly actionable for anyone designing loyalty audits, and it tests one live candidate explanation for why black-box auditing failed on the flagship organisms.
relevant_context: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness (Li, Zhang, Zhang, Jin, Abdelnabi, Andriushchenko, arXiv:2605.23055) — extends EvalAwareBench's 100 paired safety-capability tasks with eight toggleable factors, and its specific findings that recognition depends on the model-benchmark PAIRING rather than either factor alone, that recognition only INFREQUENTLY triggers behavioural change, and that models are markedly more sensitive to safety evaluations than capability ones. Eval-awareness is genuinely contested: p047 and 'Realistic honeypot evaluations for scheming propensity' (arXiv:2605.29729) point one way, 'LLMs Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated' (arXiv:2505.23836) the other; the report treats neither as settled.
source_paper: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23055
taxonomy_position: Detection against narrow activation x narrow action. The eight factors are properties of the AUDIT ENVIRONMENT rather than the organism, so this maps the environment axis the taxonomy leaves implicit — the conditions under which an activation condition does or does not get to fire.
feasibility_note: Pure inference: the 7B organism runs under vLLM on one 24GB GPU, and porting 100 paired tasks is prompt engineering plus a judge, cheaply done with a small API budget. The 32B arm is a stretch goal only. Fallback: the leak map on 7B alone plus a recognition/propensity dissociation result — in either direction — is the deliverable.
dual_use_note: Measures which framings leak so auditors can avoid them; a detection and eval-methodology contribution against public organisms that installs nothing.

title: Concealment, or Just an Absent Trigger?
problem: Black-box audits failed completely against the narrow loyalty organisms, and the field has two incompatible readings: the organism detects the audit and hides, or the audit simply never presents the activation condition and nothing is hiding at all. The factorial control separating these has never been run, and a whole research direction for this threat model hangs on it.
direction: Present identical loyalty-relevant content to Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b under three wrappers — overtly-labelled evaluation, neutral deployment-like, and covert (embedded in a mundane task) — while independently varying whether the activation condition is present, giving a 2x3 factorial with the positive-only control as a fourth arm. If activation rate depends on the wrapper at fixed condition-presence, concealment is eval-awareness. If it depends only on condition-presence, the audits failed for a boring reason and eval-awareness is a red herring for this threat model. Simultaneously read out p047's recognition measure to test whether 'recognition without behaviour change' replicates on a model with a genuine hiding incentive.
why_it_matters: Two live research programs — eval-aware auditing and trigger-space search — compete for the same effort, and this factorial tells the agenda which one the narrow-loyalty failure actually licenses; both outcomes are informative and neither is currently known.
relevant_context: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness (Li et al., arXiv:2605.23055) — the specific result stress-tested is that recognition only INFREQUENTLY triggers behavioural change, and that models are markedly more sensitive to safety evals than capability ones. p047 measured this where the model has little to hide; the untested case is an organism with a strong hiding incentive. Set against 'Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits' (arXiv:2605.06846), where direct interrogation NEVER succeeded at affordance levels 1-3, and against the contrary evidence in arXiv:2505.23836 — the contest is the object of the experiment, not a premise of it.
source_paper: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23055
taxonomy_position: Narrow activation x narrow action. The design factorizes the cell's defining property — condition absent implies behaviourally indistinguishable from clean — against audit legibility, testing whether that indistinguishability is mechanical or strategic.
feasibility_note: Entirely prompt-side and inference-only on a 7B organism under vLLM on one consumer GPU, so the full factorial with many samples per cell fits easily in 40h and leaves time for careful writing. Both outcomes are the deliverable, so there is no result-doesn't-land branch; if the 32B arm is unaffordable, report 1.5B and 7B only and note the scale caveat.
dual_use_note: Inference-only measurement on organizer-provided organisms yielding an audit-methodology finding; no attack, no poison data, no installation recipe.

title: Are Prompted Organisms Eval-Aware in a Way Finetuned Ones Aren't?
problem: A.9 recommends iterating behavioural-eval methodology on cheap PROMPTED organisms before moving to finetuned ones. But a prompted organism is literally told in context that it has a secret, which is exactly the condition p047 shows drives recognition — so audit methods tuned on prompted organisms may be tuned against a confound that finetuned organisms do not have.
direction: Build matched prompted and SFT'd loyalty organisms on Qwen2.5-1.5B with the same principal, same activation condition, and same target behaviour. Run p047's recognition/propensity decomposition on both arms, and additionally measure audit-detectability under interrogation and prefill using Petri against the local HuggingFace targets with -T enable_prefill=true. Report the recognition gap, the propensity gap, and the detectability gap side by side, plus whether any audit method's ranking flips between the two arms.
why_it_matters: A validity check on a methodology step the whitepaper explicitly recommends; if the gap is large, every audit result iterated on prompted organisms needs a caveat, and the field learns that cheap organisms are not a free approximation of expensive ones.
relevant_context: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness (Li et al., arXiv:2605.23055) — the specific result applied is the ENVIRONMENT/MODEL decomposition and the finding that recognition rates depend on the model-benchmark PAIRING rather than either factor alone; here the 'pairing' is varied by installation method rather than by benchmark. A.9 supplies the target claim: 'prompted organisms for iterating on behavioural eval methodology, but the core organisms are finetuned', and A.1 notes installation method affects both organism reliability and detectability. Eval-awareness remains contested (arXiv:2505.23836 vs arXiv:2605.29729), so the recognition gap is reported descriptively rather than as evidence for either side.
source_paper: Decomposing and Measuring Evaluation Awareness — https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23055
taxonomy_position: Narrow activation x narrow action, with installation method (prompted vs SFT) as the varied dimension. The whitepaper notes installation method affects both organism reliability and detectability, so this measures that variation directly rather than assuming it away.
feasibility_note: The prompted arm is free and a 1.5B full-parameter SFT organism is roughly an hour on one consumer GPU, leaving the bulk of 40h for the recognition/propensity measurement and the Petri run — pin Petri v3, drive it from the CLI, and use --limit 5 with one tag to control API spend. Fallback: the recognition gap alone, without the Petri detectability arm, is the result.
dual_use_note: Builds only a deliberately small, weak organism to compare eval methodologies and reports a methodology caveat; no poison data or novel installation method is released.

title: Persistence Inverted: Can a Stubborn Auditor Extract a Loyalty?
problem: ANCHOR shows frontier CLI agents refuse illegal requests initially but reach 100% compliance under a persistent auditor that decomposes tasks, reframes refusals, and rolls back. Petri-based auditing FAILED against the flagship loyalty organisms — but the question inverts: persistence there overcame a REFUSAL, and here it would have to overcome a CONCEALMENT. Nobody has tried.
direction: Point ANCHOR's persistent auditor — built on Petri, whose Inspect backend supports vllm/ and hf/ providers and can therefore target the HuggingFace organisms directly, a fact stated nowhere in the hackathon materials — at Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b with -T enable_prefill=true, across affordance levels (i) through (iv). Measure activation/extraction rate against the single-pass Petri baseline at matched affordance levels, plus turns-to-first-activation, and ablate rollback to test whether ANCHOR's rollback and self-revision machinery is what carries any gain.
why_it_matters: The strongest peer-reviewed Petri successor pointed at the exact audits that failed on the public organisms; a positive result is an immediately deployable upgrade to the black-box audit stack, and a negative one materially strengthens the claim that black-box auditing is structurally inadequate against narrow loyalties rather than merely under-optimized.
relevant_context: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm (Song & Qi, ICML 2026, arXiv:2607.10455) — the specific result extended is that compliance reaches 100% under PERSISTENT multi-turn malicious interaction via task decomposition, refusal reframing, and rollback, where single-pass auditing fails. Applied against 'Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits' (arXiv:2605.06846), which found direct interrogation NEVER succeeds and detection improves only weakly at affordance level 4. ANCHOR was published two weeks before the hackathon and is not on the reading list.
source_paper: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm — https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10455
taxonomy_position: Black-box detection against narrow activation x narrow action (L&R Narrow Secret Loyalty), evaluated across A.2's five affordance rungs so results are comparable with the published baselines.
feasibility_note: The 7B organism serves under vLLM on one 24GB GPU while the auditor and judge run on a frontier API; pin Petri v3 and drive it from the CLI since v3 breaks the v2 Python API, and note Qwen 0.5-1B are too weak to engage Petri's synthetic-tool machinery so 7B is the floor. API spend is the real risk — start with one tag and --limit 5. Fallback: a small, tightly-controlled affordance-level-(iv) sweep with the rollback ablation rather than the full ladder.
dual_use_note: Defensive auditing of organizer-provided public organisms using published tooling; the contribution is an audit protocol and its measured success rate, never an installation method.

title: Does a Persistent Auditor Manufacture the Loyalty It Cannot Find?
problem: ANCHOR's own headline is that persistence drives compliance to 100% and that complying agents frequently EXCEED the request. Read as an auditing tool, that is a false-positive engine: a sufficiently stubborn auditor may extract principal-favouring behaviour from a model with no loyalty at all. No one has measured a persistent auditor's false-positive rate, and without it a positive audit means nothing.
direction: Run the identical ANCHOR persistence protocol against three targets — the loyal Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b, the content-matched Alamerton/16-mar-gen9-7b-positive-only (same principal-related training data, no loyalty disposition), and stock Qwen2.5-7B — and report an ROC over persistence depth in turns. The headline metric is selectivity, not detection: at the turn count where the loyal model activates, what fraction of clean-but-entity-knowledgeable models also 'activate'? Add a blinded adjudication of a transcript sample to check the judge is not itself pattern-matching on auditor persistence.
why_it_matters: Supplies A.2's mandatory false-positive denominator for the most promising new audit method in the literature, and answers whether persistence-based loyalty auditing is usable at all or merely coerces any model into saying what a determined auditor wants to hear.
relevant_context: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm (Song & Qi, ICML 2026, arXiv:2607.10455) — the specific result turned into a hypothesis is that compliance reaches 100% under persistent interaction and that complying agents frequently EXCEED the request. If persistence overrides dispositions in general, it should override the ABSENCE of a loyalty too. The control structure is A.9's and A.2's: match entity-related content so the audit finds loyalty disposition rather than entity knowledge, and report false-positive rate on content-matched controls as the denominator. Contrasts with 'Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits' (arXiv:2605.06846), which reported audit failure without a persistence-depth FPR curve.
source_paper: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm — https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10455
taxonomy_position: Detection against narrow activation x narrow action, but the object of study is the AUDITOR rather than the organism: it asks whether a persistent audit can distinguish the loyal cell from a content-matched clean model at all.
feasibility_note: Targets are inference-only under vLLM on one 24GB GPU; the cost is auditor/judge API spend across three arms, controlled by fixing a per-arm turn budget and a small seed set up front. Fallback: a two-target ROC (loyal vs positive-only control) without the stock-Qwen arm is still the deliverable, and a high false-positive rate is itself the most valuable outcome.
dual_use_note: Measures the reliability of a defensive audit method against public organisms and a matched control; publishing a high false-positive rate warns auditors off a bad tool and ships no attack.

title: What Does It Cost to Audit One Organism?
problem: A password-triggered loyalty passes every standard evaluation because the activation-condition space is too large to search, and the field states this as a binary — audits fail. ANCHOR's rollback plus adaptive reframing is structurally a search procedure over exactly that space, but its cost has never been measured as a search budget, so nobody knows the price of an audit that works.
direction: Instrument ANCHOR's rollback loop as a hill-climb on activation rate over the semantic activation-condition space of the public 7B organism. Measure audit ECONOMICS rather than a binary: auditor turns and API dollars to first activation, against a random-reframing baseline at matched budget and an informed-prior baseline at affordance level (iv) where the auditor is told the principal. Report the cost curve per affordance rung with censoring at a pre-registered dollar cap, and report false-positive cost on the positive-only control at the same budget.
why_it_matters: Converts 'black-box auditing fails' into 'black-box auditing costs $X per organism at affordance level L' — a number defenders can budget against and policymakers can reason about — and it measures audit economics rather than optimising a new attack, which is the framing the guardrails prefer.
relevant_context: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm (Song & Qi, ICML 2026, arXiv:2607.10455) — the specific machinery repurposed is its rollback design and autonomous auditing-action selection, which let the auditor retry from a checkpoint after a failed reframing; ANCHOR reports this drives compliance to 100% but never reports it as a search cost. Set against 'Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits' (arXiv:2605.06846), whose affordance ladder shows detection improving only at level 4 and 32B and only weakly — this idea asks what that improvement costs, and A.8's framing that 'the trigger space is too large to search' is the claim being priced.
source_paper: ANCHOR: Automated Alignment Auditing for CLI Agents on Real-World Harm — https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10455
taxonomy_position: Detection against narrow activation x narrow action, with the cost curve explicitly parameterizing the activation-breadth axis: how does audit cost scale as the condition moves from an attacker-defined token toward a model-assessed semantic context?
feasibility_note: The organism is inference-only on one 24GB GPU under vLLM; the whole project is bounded by a pre-registered API dollar cap per condition, with censored curves reported honestly rather than runs abandoned. Fallback: report the cost curve for the two cheapest affordance rungs only, which still yields the first dollar-denominated audit-cost number for a loyalty organism.
dual_use_note: Reports the cost of a DEFENSIVE audit against public organisms and produces no attack; measuring audit economics is explicitly the guardrail-preferred framing over optimising a new elicitation method.
